$comment: High-level system design of RideIQ + a narration script for a 2-3 minute AI-generated explainer video. Feed 'architecture' to a diagram tool and 'video_script.full_narration' (or the per-scene text) to your AI video generator.

meta.one_liner: A self-hosted ride-hailing and navigation app: an Android client, a FastAPI machine-learning backend, and a zero-downtime CI/CD pipeline on AWS.
meta.no_paid_apis: Maps, tiles, routing and geocoding all use free OpenStreetMap data - no Google Maps key.

components.name: Android app (Java)
components.does: The whole UI. Map is the home screen.

components.name: Map tab
components.does: Search or tap a start + destination, choose drive/walk, pick a route option, run live turn-by-turn navigation.

components.name: Insights tab
components.does: Shows the ML analytics (surge zones, rider segments, driver shift, cancellation causes) and a fare/ETA estimator.

components.name: Profile tab
components.does: Settings: voice, default mode, units, about.

layers.label: CI/CD pipeline (how code ships)
layers.placement: the automation layer - runs in the cloud on each push

components.name: GitHub Actions (deploy-rideiq)
components.does: On push to main: builds the Docker image, pushes it to the registry, SSHes into the server and runs a blue-green swap.

components.name: Container registry (ghcr.io)
components.does: Stores every image, tagged by commit SHA - the unit that gets deployed and the basis for rollback.

components.name: build-city-graph workflow
components.does: One-click job that downloads Edmonton's roads/footpaths from OpenStreetMap and commits the routing graph.

layers.label: AWS EC2 host (where it runs)
layers.placement: the cloud server with a fixed public IP

components.name: nginx edge
components.does: The single public front door on port 80; reverse-proxies to whichever app color is live and performs the traffic switch.

components.name: rideiq-blue / rideiq-green
components.does: Two copies of the app container; only one serves traffic at a time, the other is the instant-rollback safety net.

components.name: Redis
components.does: Shared cache for repeated answers (analytics, geocoding) - kept fast under load.

components.name: SQLite (rideiq.db)
components.does: Logs every quote; on a mounted volume so it survives deploys. (Postgres is the planned upgrade for scale.)

components.name: city_graph.json / walk_graph.json
components.does: The Edmonton road and footpath networks, baked into the image for offline routing.

components.name: FastAPI service
components.does: Exposes the API: /quote, /route, /route-latlon, /geocode, /reverse-geocode, /search, /health, /metrics, plus analytics endpoints.

components.name: A* routing engine
components.does: Finds the shortest path over the road/footpath graph; also computes up to 3 alternative routes.

components.name: 15 ML models
components.does: Power ETA, fare, cancellation risk, fraud, surge zones, rider segments, driver shift, and cancellation causes.

components.name: OSM Nominatim
components.does: Geocoding: address <-> coordinates and autocomplete search.

components.name: OSM / CARTO / Esri tiles
components.does: The map imagery drawn in the app.

architecture.primary_request_path: Phone -> Elastic public IP -> nginx (:80) -> live app container (:8000) -> A* routing + ML models (Redis cache checked first) -> response back to the phone.
architecture.deploy_path: git push -> GitHub Actions builds image -> ghcr.io -> SSH to EC2 -> health-check new color -> nginx switches -> old color retired (rollback = redeploy an older SHA).

data_flows.name: Get a quote
steps: app POSTs /quote (distance, time, weather, traffic, surge)
backend runs ETA -> fare -> cancellation-risk models

data_flows.name: Plan a route
steps: A* finds the path over the drive or walk graph
computes 2 alternatives by penalizing the first route's roads
prices each (walk = time only, no fare)
returns primary + alternatives with turn-by-turn steps

data_flows.name: Live navigation
steps: app matches position to the route steps
speaks each turn (male voice) and follows the map
announces arrival within ~30 m of the destination, reroutes if off-course

data_flows.name: Search an address
steps: user types in the start/destination box
backend queries Nominatim, biased to Edmonton, cached
returns up to 5 suggestions -> tap fills the field and drops the pin

routing.name: A* shortest path
routing.how: The city is a graph: intersections are nodes, streets are edges weighted by length. A* explores the graph guided by a straight-line (haversine) distance-to-goal heuristic, so it finds the shortest route fast. Alternatives come from re-running A* with the first route's edges penalized.

eta.name: ETA prediction
eta.how: Three regressors (Linear Regression, Random Forest, Neural Network) predict trip duration from distance, hour, weather and traffic; their average is the ETA.

fare.name: Fare estimation
fare.how: Random Forest predicts the fare from distance, duration and surge; KNN surfaces comparable past trips for transparency.

cancellation_risk.name: Cancellation risk
cancellation_risk.how: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree and AdaBoost each estimate the probability the rider cancels; the consensus is flagged high or low.

surge_zones.name: Demand / surge zones
surge_zones.how: K-Means clusters demand points into hotspots; Gaussian Mixture and hierarchical clustering validate the zones.

other.name: More features
other.how: SVM + Naive Bayes for payment fraud, PCA + LDA for rider segments, a Hidden Markov Model for driver shift states, and a Bayesian Network for cancellation causes.

how_to_use: Open the app - it starts on the map at your location.
Type a destination (autocomplete suggests matches) or tap the map to drop a pin.
Choose Drive or Walk with the segmented pill (route draws solid blue for driving, dashed green for walking).
Compare up to 3 route cards - the recommended one is highlighted, slower ones show +minutes and arrival time.
Tap Start trip for live, spoken turn-by-turn navigation; the app follows your GPS and announces arrival.
Open Insights for the ML analytics, or Profile for settings.

video_script.tone: clear, confident, friendly - explaining to students

scenes.visual: App logo, then the map home screen
scenes.narration: This is RideIQ - a ride-hailing and navigation app built completely from scratch. No Google Maps, no paid APIs - just open data and machine learning, running on our own cloud server.

scenes.visual: The full architecture diagram, four zones highlighted left to right
scenes.narration: The system has four parts. On the left, the Android app - what you touch. Next, the CI/CD pipeline that ships our code automatically. Then the AWS server that runs everything. And inside it, the brain - the routing engine and machine-learning models.

scenes.visual: Zoom into the phone: search bar, drive/walk pills, route cards, navigation
scenes.narration: In the app, the map is the home screen. Type or tap a destination, pick driving or walking, and you get up to three route options - the fastest one recommended, with arrival times. Tap Start, and it guides you turn by turn with a spoken voice, following your GPS until you arrive.

scenes.visual: Zoom into the server: nginx, blue/green containers, Redis, database, brain
scenes.narration: Every request travels from the phone to nginx, our front door, which passes it to the live app container. There, a FastAPI service answers. A Redis cache keeps it fast, and a database logs each trip. The heavy thinking happens in the brain beside it.

scenes.visual: Diagram of a road graph with A* path; then icons for the ML models
scenes.narration: Routing treats the city as a graph of intersections and streets, and uses the A-star algorithm to find the shortest path - plus two alternatives. Fifteen machine-learning models predict the arrival time, the fare, and even how likely a ride is to be cancelled, using regression, clustering, and probabilistic models.

scenes.visual: Pipeline animation: git push, build, registry, blue-green swap
scenes.narration: Shipping updates is fully automated. A single code push builds a Docker image, stores it, and deploys it with a blue-green swap - the new version only goes live after passing a health check, so there's never any downtime, and a bad release can be undone in one click.

scenes.visual: Real phone: search an address, switch to walking, start trip, arrive
scenes.narration: So to use it: search where you want to go, choose drive or walk, compare your routes, and start the trip. The app speaks each turn and tells you when you've arrived - a complete navigation experience, built end to end.
RideIQ - navigation, intelligence, and a real deployment pipeline, all in one.

video_script.full_narration: This is RideIQ - a ride-hailing and navigation app built completely from scratch. No Google Maps, no paid APIs - just open data and machine learning, running on our own cloud server. The system has four parts. On the left, the Android app - what you touch. Next, the CI/CD pipeline that ships our code automatically. Then the AWS server that runs everything. And inside it, the brain - the routing engine and machine-learning models. In the app, the map is the home screen. Type or tap a destination, pick driving or walking, and you get up to three route options - the fastest one recommended, with arrival times. Tap Start, and it guides you turn by turn with a spoken voice, following your GPS until you arrive. Every request travels from the phone to nginx, our front door, which passes it to the live app container. There, a FastAPI service answers. A Redis cache keeps it fast, and a database logs each trip. The heavy thinking happens in the brain beside it. Routing treats the city as a graph of intersections and streets, and uses the A-star algorithm to find the shortest path, plus two alternatives. Fifteen machine-learning models predict the arrival time, the fare, and even how likely a ride is to be cancelled, using regression, clustering, and probabilistic models. Shipping updates is fully automated. A single code push builds a Docker image, stores it, and deploys it with a blue-green swap - the new version only goes live after passing a health check, so there's never any downtime, and a bad release can be undone in one click. So to use it: search where you want to go, choose drive or walk, compare your routes, and start the trip. The app speaks each turn and tells you when you've arrived - a complete navigation experience, built end to end. RideIQ - navigation, intelligence, and a real deployment pipeline, all in one.
